first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and prior evidence indicates that shortening onboarding and reducing signup friction improve early activation and time-to-value. A small guarded test is preferable to promotional pricing, which previously harmed 30-day retention; monitor qualified conversion and downstream retention to ensure friction reduction does not lower lead quality.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding, prioritizing the simultaneous declines in completion and activation. The verified onboarding result improved completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, making it the strongest sustainable-revenue option. Do not broadly remove signup fields yet: that result was SMB-specific and included a 1% retention decline. Measure activation, qualified revenue, and 30-day retention by segment.

final2.rationale: Keep the approved onboarding experiment rather than switching to broad promotional pricing. The verified shortening result improved completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, directly addressing current activation and onboarding declines. Although deeper competitor pricing increases SMB pressure, promotional pricing previously reduced 30-day retention and threatens sustainable qualified revenue. Monitor SMB win-back and qualified revenue as secondary outcomes, with retention and churn guardrails.
